Commissioner of Taxes, Intelligence and Investigation Zone ------ Respondent
full_judgment: 6. On a perusal of the order of the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes it also appears that he like the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes do not find any fault with the method of accounting. But relying on the previous assessment, orders reduced the receipts from commission receipts from Taka 15,000 per person to Taka 8.000 per person and modified the assessment order accordingly. Here also the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes failed to appreciate the legal aspect of the case and failed to appreciate that the method of accounting regularly employed by the assesse was followed in the instant assessment year. In the instant case, the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes does not arrive at a finding that the income, profits and gains of the assesse cannot be properly reduced therefrom. It is therefore, clear that the method of accounting regularly employed by the assesse cannot arbitrarily be rejected by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes and employ his own method and losing sight of this aspect illegally relied on the previous assessment orders and reduced the receipts from Taka 15,000 to Taka 8,000 most illegally and on a perusal of the order of the Appellate Tribunal it appears that in the instant case the Appellate Tribunal also without applying their minds to the facts and circumstances of the case mechanically affirmed the order of the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes in ignorance of the legal provision as contained in section 13A(1) & (3) of the Income Tax Act, 1922. In this connection it may be stated that the assesse applicant is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913. While submitting their return they have complied with the provisions of section 13A(1) and (3) of the Act and a legal presumption is attached to the Certificate issued by the Chartered Accountant and in the instant case there is no material on record to rebut the legal presumption as to the correctness of the audited account of the applicant company and this aspect of the case was also lost sight of by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes as well as by the Appellate Tribunal. It, thus appears that the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes. Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes as well as Taxes Appellate Tribunal in gross violation of the provisions of sections 13 and 13A (1) and (3) of the Act most illegally merely on surmises and conjectures resorted to estimate the commission receipts of the applicant company and as such the order of the Appellate Tribunal cannot be sustained in law and as such the order of the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes and the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes also suffers from gross infirmity. We, therefore, answer the question No. 1 as raised in paragraph 14 of the application in the negative and in favour of the applicant.
